cassia.predicted_cell_type: Hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs) — CD34+ primitive hematopoietic stem/progenitor cell cluster
strengths: Correctly identifies CD34+ HSPC/HSC identity using CD34, PROM1, GATA2, HOXA9, HOXA10, MYB, PBX1, ALDH1A1
Interprets basophil/mast and megakaryocyte genes as multilineage priming rather than commitment
Proposes CL:0000037, consistent with the dominant marker program
weaknesses: Top1 free-text label has no exact CL mapping; rank2 composite label over-specifies LT-HSC/MPP/pre-BMP
LT-HSC emphasis is weakened by proliferation-associated genes CDK6, TYMS, NPDC1

strengths: Ontology-valid ancestor consistent with HSPC identity
weaknesses: Under-specific; misses the supported stem-cell identity
Does not capture CD34/AVP/CRHBP stemness signal

clusterProfiler.predicted_cell_type: Hematopoietic Stem/Progenitor Cell (HSPC) / Early Myeloid Progenitor
strengths: Recognizes HSPC core using CD34, PROM1, CRHBP, SPINK2, PRSS57
Correctly notes absence of mature lineage markers
weaknesses: Top1 unmapped; candidates include non-hierarchical lineage-restricted/oligopotent progenitors without direct branch-specific evidence
Early myeloid/committed-progenitor components are not supported by the primitive HSC marker program

supporting: CD34, AVP, CRHBP, GATA2, HOXA9, HOXA10, MYB, PBX1, ALDH1A1, SPINK2, PRSS57 support HSC identity over generic hematopoietic precursor cell
CD34 and GATA2 plus absence of mature lineage markers (CD3D, CD19, MS4A1, NKG7, CD14, LYZ) support the CD34+ HSPC branch
PMID 36658547 allowed as supporting literature context for CD34+ HSPC identity
conflicting: Proliferation/MPP-associated genes CDK6, TYMS, NPDC1 and basophil/mast/megakaryocyte priming genes complicate an LT-HSC-specific call but do not overturn HSC identity
Enrichment candidates CL:0002031/CL:0002032 are non-hierarchical to HSC and lack direct branch-specific support
enrichment_or_literature: Allowed literature (PMID 36658547) supports CD34+ HSPC interpretation
Reactome/GO terms such as Hemostasis, GPCR signalling, and Transcriptional regulation of granulopoiesis are consistent with an HSPC state but not lineage-specific
